lead: A personal assistant written from scratch in Python, small on purpose: it talks to you on Telegram, remembers your conversations and uses a model in the cloud or local. You stop opening a website to chat: the assistant is yours.
objetivo: design, install and put to work an assistant with memory and a personality you define.

aprende.t: Design the assistant before you install it

secoes.sub: From Telegram to the model and back.

nos.detalhe: You chat on Telegram, on your phone or computer, just like with any other contact.
The bot is the front door. You create it in @BotFather with /newbot and keep the token only in .env, as you learned in step 1.
INTELECTO receives the message, adds the personality and what it remembers about you, and builds the request to the model. It's small on purpose, so you can understand it and change it.
The model generates the answer. In the cloud (OpenRouter) it's stronger and costs per use; local (Ollama) runs on your computer, if it can handle it.

secoes.volta: The answer goes back to the same Telegram chat
secoes.legenda: Want to see other ready-to-install assistant systems? The JARVIS area of Eventos has several.

rolagem_fim.texto: You write on Telegram, INTELECTO adds the personality and memory, the model answers, and the answer goes back to the same chat. All yours, with the token kept in .env.

texto: Before you install, write down who the assistant is: name, way of talking, three things it should do every week, three it should never do, and what it needs to remember about you.
This file answers the installation questions.

exemplo.texto: Someone else reads the file and understands who your assistant is.

texto: On Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, and choose a name and a @username.
Keep the token only in the .env.

exemplo.texto: The token does not appear in any file other than the .env.

texto: Clone INTELECTO, export your briefing on the comparison page, and ask Claude Code or Codex to build from it and from doc/intelecto.md, with tests.
Use the answers from your meu-jarvis.md. The full walkthrough is in lesson 4 of the step 2 course.

exemplo.texto: You send "hi" and it replies with the name and the style you set.

texto: Tell it three facts about yourself in one day, and ask about them the next day, in a new conversation.
Then turn one task from your week into a standing request and use it for five days in a row.

exemplo.texto: Every morning, when I send "dia", list my three priorities based on what I told you yesterday.

secoes.sub: Copy the template, fill it in, and only then install.

abas.html:
1. The Telegram token (from @BotFather), only in the .env.
  2. The model: in the cloud (OpenRouter) or local (Ollama).
  3. The personality: your meu-jarvis.md.

Run the same question on both and note it in a table:

  • Response time
  • Quality of the answer
  • Cost per use

The goal is to know, with your own numbers, which model to use for what.

secoes.fonte: Full exercises: jornada-agentes/exercicios/02-jarvis.md. The extra challenge (the task list you send before going to sleep) is the entry point for step 3.

secoes.sub: INTELECTO on Telegram, with memory and personality.
The explanation appears after your answer.

opcoes: Because the installation doesn't work without it.
Because it defines the name, style, limits, and what to remember, and it answers the installation questions.
perguntas.explica: The design comes first: with the name, style, what to do, and what never to do written down, you answer the guided setup without improvising, and you have a way to judge whether the assistant is right.

perguntas.p: The assistant didn't remember what you told it yesterday. What's the first step?
opcoes: Check in the course how memory is stored and adjust it.
perguntas.explica: Exercise E4 says exactly that: if it doesn't remember, check in the INTELECTO course how memory is stored and adjust it.

perguntas.p: When does a local model (Ollama) make sense?
opcoes: When your computer can handle it and your numbers for time, quality, and cost show it's worth it.
perguntas.explica: The choice is measured: the same question to both, a table with time, quality, and cost, and a decision based on your numbers.
